talk: Churn is fans who don't come back. It's the slow puncture in every subscription business. You can sign new fans all summer and still go backwards if the old ones keep walking out.

terms.meaning: Share of customers who leave in a period.
The opposite of churn. The share who stay.

questions.prompt: You have 10,000 season ticket holders. 15% don't renew, and you sign 1,200 new ones. Where do you end up?
whyNot: 10,000 - 1,500 = 8,500 counts the leavers but forgets the 1,200 new fans.
Nothing stays still. 1,500 left and 1,200 joined, so 1,500 - 1,200 = 300 fewer than you started.

questions.prompt: Next year you want 10,500 holders, starting from 10,000, with 10% churn. How many new fans must you sign?
questions.hint: Replace the leavers first, then add the growth.
working: 10,000 x 10% = 1,000 leave, so you sign 1,000 just to stand still.
1,000 + 500 = 1,500 new fans. All that to grow 500 / 10,000 = 5%.
whyNot: 500 is the growth you want, but first you have to replace the 1,000 who leave.
1,000 only replaces the leavers. You'd end the year where you started, at 10,000.
10,000 - 1,000 + 2,000 = 11,000, which is 500 more than your target.

questions.prompt: Each holder is worth $600 a year. You cut churn from 15% to 10% on 10,000 fans. What's that worth a year?
questions.hint: How many fans did you keep?
working: Keeping 500 fans is often cheaper than winning 500 new ones.
whyNot: 100 x $600 = $60,000 counts 100 fans kept. You keep 500.
500 x $300 = $150,000 values each fan at half a year. Each holder is worth $600 a year.
1,000 x $600 = $600,000 counts 1,000 fans kept, as if churn fell by 10 points. It fell by 5 points, from 15% to 10%.

penalty.prompt: You have {start} season ticket holders. {churn} don't renew, and you sign {signed} new ones. How many do you end up with?
penalty.hint: Start, minus the leavers, plus the new ones.

traps.why: You forgot the {start * churn|int} who didn't renew.

call.title: Renewal season
call.prompt: Renewal letters go out next week. Last year 15% of holders didn't renew. You have $30,000. A renewal push (early-bird perks, calls to lapsed fans) should keep 400 who'd otherwise leave. Ads for new fans should win 150.

options.label: Run the renewal push
options.result: Good call. 400 x $18 = $7,200 a matchday kept, so $30,000 / $7,200 = about 4 matchdays to earn it back. Keeping fans is cheaper than finding new ones.

options.label: Spend it on ads for new fans
options.result: 150 x $18 = $2,700 a matchday. It takes $30,000 / $2,700 = about 11 matchdays to earn it back.

options.label: Do nothing
options.result: 8,000 x 15% = 1,200 fans could walk, and you did nothing to stop it.

takeaway: Plug the leak before you pour in more fans.
